title: An 8-Inch Hailstone Fell on South Dakota. Two Pounds of Ice

scenes.text: An 8 inch hailstone fell on South Dakota. Two pounds of ice.
July 2010. Vivian, South Dakota. A ranch hand picked it up.
Eight inches across. Nearly two pounds. America's biggest ever.
The power was out for hours, so it melted in his freezer. He says it was bigger when it landed.
Hail that size falls at over 100 miles an hour.
A supercell's updraft kept throwing it back up into freezing air, layer on layer, until the wind couldn't hold two pounds.

description:
On July 23, 2010, a hailstone 8 inches across and almost two pounds fell on Vivian, South Dakota, the largest ever measured in the United States.
Ranch hand Leslie Scott found it and froze it, but a power cut let it melt for hours before NOAA measured it, so it was probably bigger when it landed. Hail over 4 inches can fall at more than 100 miles an hour. Stones that size form when a supercell's updraft keeps lifting them back into freezing air, adding layer after layer.
What's the biggest hail you've ever seen? Comment below.
first_comment: Hail this size needs an updraft strong enough to hold a two-pound rock of ice in the air. Would you run for the car or stay inside?
